images.title: 126 km in 2.5 hours
images.purpose: Show that 126 km in 2.5 hours means 50.4 km in each hour, so the average speed is 50.4 km per hour.
images.composition: One long horizontal bar across the centre split into three parts, with brackets above and below and one equation line at the bottom; generous white space.
exact_structure: One horizontal bar, total label 126 km above it with a grey #6B7280 bracket spanning the whole bar.
The bar is split into 3 parts with lengths in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1: part 1 teal #0072B2, part 2 teal #0072B2, part 3 amber #E69F00 (half the length of a teal part).
Inside the parts: 50.4 km, 50.4 km, 25.2 km.
Under the parts: 1 hour, 1 hour, half hour.
Bottom centre: one line 126 ÷ 2.5 = 50.4 km per hour, with 50.4 in reddish purple #CC79A7.
rejection: parts not in the length ratio 2 : 2 : 1
images.takeaway: Average speed is the distance for one hour: 126 ÷ 2.5 = 50.4 km per hour, and 50.4 + 50.4 + 25.2 = 126.
images.description: A bar for 126 km split into two 1 hour parts of 50.4 km and a half hour part of 25.2 km, with 126 ÷ 2.5 = 50.4 km per hour.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on Ravi's average speed.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to add the three parts to check they make 126 km.

image_decisions.why: A bar model shows what dividing by 2.5 hours means before the fraction method.
